answer: An agent economy can price identity like an orchard prices fruit: trust grows only from a long, verifiable history of useful work. Each agent carries a unique pigment of behavior, its signed task record, which cannot be copied cheaply. New identities start with tiny limits, and every successful job raises the cap in a slow spiral, while one proven fraud burns the whole stake. Making a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand real histories, and the attacker pays in time and locked funds before earning anything.
